To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
carbon‐starvation stress induces general resistance in E. coli, and that the molecular basis for this resistance is the induction of stress proteins.
carbon‐starvation resistance is mediated through the induction of the pex genes and that these genes are involved in the synthesis of stress proteins.
carbon‐starvation resistance in Eschericia coli is a complex phenomenon that involves a temporally ordered induction of 40–80 starvation genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and analysis of starvation and stress genes and their products.
the elucidation of the molecular basis of the development of general resistance in E. coli and the identification of the genes responsible.
elucidating the molecular basis of starvation resistance in E. coli, and the potential applications of the findings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the starvation response is a general stress response.
starvation resistance is a complex phenomenon involving many genes and regulatory mechanisms, some of which are still not fully elucidated.
starvation‐induced general stress resistance is the result of a complex, temporally ordered program involving at least 40–80 different genes, some of which utilize minor sigma factors for induction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

carbon starvation is a potent physiological stress that induces a complex and temporally ordered program for the expression of genes involved in escape from starvation, and for the development of a general resistance to other stresses.

carbon starvation in E. coli is an important stress response that is not just a consequence of growth limitation.
